I quit my job in February without a plan, which in hindsight was a little stupid, but I'd been miserable for about a year and kept telling myself the next reorg would fix it. It didn't. Three reorgs in a row, actually.

The first month was fine, mostly because I was still running on the adrenaline of having quit. The second month was worse. I applied to nine jobs and heard back from one, and that one rejected me after a panel interview that I thought went well. My partner was very patient about this, more patient than I would have been.

What actually helped wasn't networking advice or resume tips, it was a former coworker texting me out of nowhere to ask if I wanted to grab coffee, and that turning into a referral three weeks later. I don't think there's a lesson in that beyond "keep in touch with people you liked working with," which is not exactly a strategy, just something that happened to work.

I start the new job Monday. I'm nervous about it in a way I wasn't expecting to be.
